name: GitHub
approach: Useful README, working quickstart, example project and release notes
measure: Repository traffic plus downstream successful installs/use
risk: Stars can come from curiosity; rolling traffic history is short
complexity: Low; public metrics or repository-scoped read token
maintainability: Keep examples tested and collect traffic weekly

name: Show HN
approach: Tryable substantive project, maker explanation and thoughtful replies
measure: Thread feedback and tagged product activation
risk: One-off generated projects and signup-only pages may be ineligible
complexity: Low setup; launch timing and discussion are unpredictable
maintainability: Be available for support; no repeated routine version posts

name: YouTube
approach: Show the payoff or a useful tutorial with a directly tryable next step
measure: Engaged viewing, tagged visits, successful first use and return
risk: Public playback starts can look impressive without product interest
complexity: Moderate production; definitions and reporting delay matter
maintainability: Batch footage; keep one reusable demonstration format

name: TikTok
approach: Show the real payoff in the first seconds as a short vertical video, with one tryable next step in the profile link or caption
measure: Video views at 100% and average play time by video length, tagged profile-link visits, first use and return
risk: Views measure attention, not first use or payment; promotional posts need the content disclosure setting; engagement tricks and bulk automation break integrity rules
complexity: Moderate: vertical production and in-app analytics that differ from the ads-side definitions
maintainability: Batch clips from real play or use; no automation, bought engagement or reposting bots

name: Facebook Groups and Pages
cost: 0 for organic posts; ads are separate spend
approach: Share one tryable link in a relevant Group under its rules, or on your own Page, and disclose any commercial relationship
measure: Tagged link visits, replies and objections, first use and return, with Page impressions or Views kept as exposure only
risk: Exposure counts overstate interest; Group promotion rules vary; very high-frequency posting, bought engagement and misleading links break the spam rules
complexity: Moderate: Group-by-Group judgment, and Meta renames and redefines its metrics
maintainability: Show up as a participant, not a poster; re-check metric names when exporting

name: X
cost: 0 for organic posts; API access and ads are separate spend
approach: Post a short demonstration with one tryable link, reply by hand to people who respond, and join an existing builder or genre conversation
measure: Replies and objections, tagged link visits, first use and return, with post impressions kept as exposure only
risk: Impressions are not unique people and say nothing about use; bulk or unsolicited replies, engagement schemes and unlabelled bots break the rules; API terms and pricing change
complexity: Low to post by hand; high if automated, because automation needs labels, consent and prior approval for some uses
maintainability: Do it by hand; no reply, like or follow automation; re-read the rules before any API use

name: Steam store page and wishlists
cost: $100 per app, recoupable after $1,000 adjusted gross revenue, plus production effort; verify current terms
approach: Publish a coming-soon page early, send tagged traffic from your other channels to it, and read wishlist additions and tracked visits per source
measure: Wishlist additions net of deletions, UTM tracked visits and wishlist conversions by source, later wishlist purchases
risk: A wishlist is intent, not payment; tracked visits only count signed-in users so they are a lower bound; there is a 30-day wait after paying the fee and a two-week minimum coming-soon period
complexity: Moderate to high: store page assets, Steamworks setup, bank and tax verification, and a review before the page goes live
maintainability: Check reports daily around launches; tag every outbound link; Valve's rules and fees change, so re-read them before committing

name: Relevant Reddit communities
approach: Inspect community rules; contribute a useful native explanation where promotion is welcome
measure: Objections, tagged use and return from the specific community
risk: Repetitive promotion can be spam; no blanket posting allowance
maintainability: Build relationships; do not run a promotional bot

name: itch.io and game communities
approach: Playable demo, genre-readable screenshots and a brief development log, with each outside link tagged so itch.io referrers and your own analytics can be compared
measure: Page views, downloads or browser plays, purchases and the referrer for each; qualified plays, completion and returning players only from the game's own telemetry
risk: Audience and device fit may differ from your intended players; itch.io reports file delivery and referrals, not how the game is played; a download counts as started, not finished
complexity: Moderate asset preparation and distribution setup
maintainability: Maintain the playable build and respond to bug reports; never sign people up to a mailing list automatically

name: Search and useful documentation
approach: Answer a real recurring question with a useful page and a working example
measure: Qualified search visits and successful use
risk: Slow feedback; ranking is not guaranteed
complexity: Instrumentation, indexable pages and topic judgment
maintainability: Update examples and monitor query intent

name: Opt-in email
approach: Useful update to people who opted in, with accurate sender details, a working unsubscribe and one clear next action
measure: Tagged successful use and unsubscribes; treat opens cautiously because mail privacy features can load tracking images without a person reading
risk: A small list limits discovery; unwanted mail harms trust and, at volume, spam complaints above provider thresholds cause blocked delivery; breaking consent or opt-out rules brings legal penalties
complexity: Consent, list care, sender authentication and deliverability
maintainability: Keep the cadence sustainable; honour unsubscribes quickly and keep a suppression list; recheck provider and legal rules, which change

name: Existing Discord community
approach: Share useful progress and invite focused feedback in a relevant existing community, as a person and with the server's permission
measure: Playtest participation, recurring use and qualitative themes, counted from your own tagged links and notes; Server Insights only where your own server qualifies
risk: Starting a new empty server creates moderation work before demand; unsolicited bulk messages, self-bots and bought or inflated engagement break Discord's rules and can end the account
maintainability: Only open your own community when you can sustain it; follow each server's rules on self-promotion

name: LinkedIn
approach: Concrete before/after workflow for the professional audience, shared as a post or in answer to a real question, with one tryable link
measure: Qualified conversations, tagged link visits and product use, with post impressions kept as exposure only
risk: Impressions and generic praise are weak demand signals; promotional invitations to strangers, repetitive messages and automation tools break the rules and can restrict the account
complexity: Requires clear professional relevance and a credible demo; analytics definitions differ between LinkedIn's own pages
maintainability: Reuse actual user stories with permission; no scraping, extensions or outreach automation

name: Product Hunt
cost: 0 for a basic launch; verify current terms
approach: Prepared maker launch with concise gallery, demo and available support
risk: Launch-day rank is not durable demand; do not solicit upvotes
maintainability: Plan support and a follow-up beyond launch day
